sections.text:
Checking 
 the Number of Pump Restarts

items:
Calculate the volume injected at each pump restart = the running time in 
 minutes x 2 (l/m).

Notice 
 from the number of restarts the rate of leakage is deduced. (A leakage of 4 
 liters per day should be investigated).

Check the oil level visually. If the level has 
 dropped the oil must be topped up and investigate the reason of the fall.

Normal: This mark corresponds to 
 the oil level when the circuit breaker is in the open position, with the 
 maximum pressure in the accumulators and a temperature of + 15 oC

Warm: This mark corresponds to the 
 oil level for the above conditions but at a temp. of +40 oC

High: At high temperatures the 
 pre-inflation pressure rises, the oil volume is reduced in the accumulators 
 and the oil level rises in the tanks.

Cold: This mark corresponds to the 
 oil level for the above conditions but at a temperature of -25 oC

Low: At low temperatures the 
 pre-inflation pressure rises, the oil volume is reduced in the accumulators 
 and the oil level lowered in the tanks.

Intermediate: At Intermediate 
 temperatures rises, the oil level should be adjusted proportionally to the 
 temperatures between warm and normal or between normal and cold.

When the oil level is checked every 12 months, 
 the temperatures should be taken into account, in order to assess whether 
 there has been any loss of oil.

When topping up the oil, use only an oil 
 complying with the required specifications.
